note: Every sum the black notebook states, as written. The Accounts tab is the ledgers' sales; these are the costs the ledgers never record — frames, insurance, paper, the studio painted, a phonograph, two watches — and the few receipts, which are hers. Declared by hand and checked against the page by scripts/framing.mjs, as the framing register is: an entry whose pattern matches nothing fails the build. Nothing is totalled, converted or adjusted, on the rule the transcriptions follow.

frames.label: Frames
frames.note: The bills and the prices, by maker.

insurance.label: Insurance
insurance.note: The Truro policies, on a page she afterwards cancelled.

household.note: What was bought, mended or painted, with what it cost.

entries.means: Four frames with insert from La Porte, Indiana — two of model 200 for the 29 x 36 and the 25 x 30, two of model 214 for the 22 x 32 and the 20 x 28 — the one bill she ruled as a table.

Order 08722 of June 25, 1955, for the Pochards' frames, model 214 at 12.05 and five of 241 in « 819 beige » at 8.30; and order 04413 of Feb. 3, 58, the same two model-200 frames as the bill, at 30.75 and 26.50 — a quarter under the bill's 26.75 for the second.
A 25 x 30, « gold, pinkish », of May 1953.
The new frames of 1952, the sums written above the Ascension and Bertram H. lines.

A family theft policy of $1000 with American Employers of Boston, taken out Dec. 18, 47 and expiring Dec. 18, 1950, at 22.50; and standard windstorm on « Cottage + Garage » for 1000. with the North British & Mercantile at 5., expiring Jan 30, 51. The whole side is cancelled with a pencil cross.

entries.term: Water colour paper, by the pound
entries.means: Cooper Union against Robinson: 72 lb at 20¢ or 23¢, 90 lb at 37¢, 140 lb at 39¢ or 50¢.

entries.term: Painting the studio and bedroom, May 1953
entries.means: « Studio + Bedroom painted 2 Coats - Casein, May 19 1953. - 4 day job », with « + bath » interlined, and the price left as a question between two figures.
A Capital bought Ap. 4, 1960 in « Even exchange for Colombia bgt. Mar 28, 60 », delivered by United Parcels and reported undelivered to Mrs. Payne at Schirmer on Ap. 19.

A Macy wrist watch bought 5, 21, 45 for $10.; a balance and a cleaning on June 2", 50 at 2.49 and 3.98, totalled 7.47 and then 7.67 — « Why? » — against a present price of $13.; the Abercrombie watch cleaned on University Place for $8.50 in Feb. 1956.
« Fountain pen - Altman - Spring 1956 - cost ? » — the one purchase she costed with a question mark.

The only money coming in that the notebook records, and it is hers: on the mailing lists of « Reality », Isabel Whitney $5. Ap. 55, Max Eastman $10., Dr. Slack - Feb $10 54, and a « $5. » in the margin of page 35.
Under the Worcester Telegram interview of Feb. 1", 1959: « Rec'd ± 1 M. Jan 27, 59 from Frank C. » Whether « 1 M. » is a sum, a month or something else is not decided here; it is given as written.
On page 112, under « 1940 » with the year written over other figures: 378.72 against « 14. », 406.08 against « 21 », and 167.70 « deduct ». What they account is not on the page.
A marginal on page 30's list of museum staff, against the Rutgers line; what is priced is not stated.
